question: With UBER closing at $63.47 in full Stage 4 breakdown just $0.47 above its $63.00 LEAPS floor, what do the multi-timeframe tape and options chain demand?

epigraph.quote: A cheap multiple cannot stop a Stage 4 breakdown when institutions are selling at 1.6x volume and the stock sits 12% below its 200-day average.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein's Stage Analysis Discipline

web_blocks.html: Fundamental quality does not override a broken tape. At the November 20, 2026 close of $63.47 (TradingView: $63.48, -3.25% on the day and -8.93% on the week), both the market-facts ledger (Stage 4) and the TradingView snapshot (STAGE_4, gate CAP_REJECTED, posture AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN) confirm an active downtrend [21, 24]. Shares now sit 31.59% below their $92.78 52-week high and hover just $0.18 above the $63.29 52-week intraday low. Every trendline slopes against buyers: -6.39% below the 20-day SMA ($67.80), -7.96% below the falling 50-day SMA ($68.96), -11.54% below the 30-week SMA ($71.76), and -12.32% below the 200-day SMA ($72.40).

Multi-timeframe inspection across Weekly (1W), Daily (1D), and 4-Hour (4H) bars shows heavy institutional distribution with zero confirmed reversal [24]. Friday's -3.25% drop printed 30.06 million shares—1.55x the 20-day average and 1.63x the 30-day average (Finviz RelVol: 1.72x). On the 4H chart, RSI has hit an oversold 29.21 beneath falling 4H 20-EMA ($67.86) and 50-SMA ($68.05) ceilings, yet intraday_4h_turn remains false. Daily RSI sits at 34.09 and Weekly RSI at 38.44, with ATR-14 expanding to $2.42 and Bollinger Band width widening to 13.58%. Meanwhile, the broader US market sits in a confirmed Downtrend (38.8% breadth above 50DMA; 10 distribution days; US 10Y yield 5.04%) [23].

web_blocks.takeaway: UBER dropped 31.59% off its high on 1.63x volume inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend. New equity bids are 0.0%. The $61.24–$63.10 band ($60.96 stop) is purely a historical support reference below the $63.00 LEAPS floor until a Stage 1 base and >$73.50 reclaim form [21, 24].

We cancel all prior short-dated call-spread ideas immediately. Do not sell puts or buy new calls into a Stage 4 liquidation.

web_blocks.title: Critical Override Audit: EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on All 5 Open Dec 17, 2027 LEAPS Contracts
paragraphs: The portfolio holds 0 common UBER shares. However, Robinhood holds 5 December 17, 2027 Call LEAPS contracts. That stack holds 4x $110 calls ($2,644.91 cost; $1,307.91 prior mark) and 1x $100 call ($818.95 cost; $467.95 prior mark). Total cost is $3,463.86 and prior mark is $1,775.86 (2.36% of $75,110.60 net worth). Remaining time is 392 calendar days as of November 20, 2026 (389 days from November 23).

Why We Tighten to EXIT_IMMEDIATELY: Both $100C and $110C hold $0.00 intrinsic value (-100%) at our $75.00 Base Case ($72.60 EV) 12 months out. Even at our $108.00 Bull Case, all 4x $110C expire at $0.00. Meanwhile, $63.47 sits just $0.47 (0.74%, <0.2x ATR-14) above $63.00 on 1.63x Stage 4 volume. Option spreads exceed 14%, and Black-Scholes delta is 0.14–0.22 (~$820–$1,020 value at 37.5%–40.0% IV). Portfolio US cash is starved at 3.38% versus the 22.0% Downtrend floor.

Binding LEAPS Rule — EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH): Close all 5 Dec 17, 2027 LEAPS contracts cleanly on market liquidity. Use limit orders near mid to curb >14% spread slippage and salvage ~$820–$1,020 into USD cash. Do not risk a gap below $63.00 or total theta decay. Execute ZERO averaging down; any print or close <= $63.00 triggers instant exit.

web_blocks.html: Two concrete chart milestones must happen before we ever reconsider UBER for new common capital. First, selling volume must dry up as shares carve a multi-week Stage 1 floor above $59.08–$62.17 (Pivot S2/S1). Second, UBER must reclaim both its 30-week SMA ($71.76) and 200-day SMA ($72.40) above $73.50 on >=1.25x average volume while S&P 500 breadth exits its Downtrend. Until both occur, capital belongs strictly on the sidelines.

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 showed you that Uber's normalized multiple is 17.1 times SBC-adjusted free cash flow rather than 12.4 times, Chapter 8 delivers the clearest possible warning from the price tape. At the November 20, 2026 close of $63.47 ($63.48 on TradingView), Uber is trapped in a full Stan Weinstein Stage 4 markdown. Shares fell 3.25% on Friday and 8.93% for the week on 30.06 million shares—1.55 times 20-day average volume and 1.63 times 30-day average volume. When institutional funds dump stock on 1.6 times normal volume at a new 52-week low ($63.29 intraday), value buyers who step in early become liquidity for forced sellers.

Every timeframe confirms that sellers remain firmly in control. On the weekly chart, Uber trades 11.54% below its 30-week moving average ($71.76) with a weekly RSI of 38.44. On the daily chart, price sits 7.96% below a falling 50-day moving average ($68.96) and 12.32% below its 200-day moving average ($72.40), with daily RSI at 34.09 and 14-day ATR widening to $2.42. Even on the 4-hour chart, where RSI has plunged to an oversold 29.21, price remains pinned below its 20-EMA ($67.86) and 50-SMA ($68.05) with zero bullish reversal trigger. Layer that on top of a broader US market Downtrend—only 38.8% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average and 10 distribution days—and fighting this tape is pure ego.

For new options trades, our verdict is equally firm: NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID and NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. Wide bid-ask spreads above 14% and a broken Stage 4 trend rule out buying new calls or spreads. Do not try to outsmart a downtrend with leverage.

That brings us to the most urgent portfolio-management decision in this report: our 5 open December 17, 2027 Call LEAPS contracts in Robinhood—4 contracts of the $110 strike ($2,644.91 cost; $1,307.91 prior mark) and 1 contract of the $100 strike ($818.95 cost; $467.95 prior mark), totaling $3,463.86 cost and $1,775.86 prior market value (2.36% of our $75,110.60 net worth) with 392 calendar days left as of November 20, 2026 (389 from November 23). Our Stage 4 override mandates EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH) across all 5 contracts.

Look at the arithmetic at $63.47. Even if Uber hits our $75.00 Base Case in 12 months, both the $100 and $110 strikes expire with $0.00 intrinsic value—a 100% loss—and even at $108.00 Bull all four $110 calls expire at zero. Meanwhile, $63.47 sits just $0.47 (less than 0.2x ATR-14) above $63.00 on 1.63x distribution volume with bid-ask spreads above 14%, Black-Scholes delta compressed to 0.14–0.22 (~$820 to $1,020 value), and portfolio cash starved at 3.38% versus our 22.0% Downtrend floor. We therefore close all 5 LEAPS contracts cleanly on market liquidity to salvage ~$820–$1,020 into USD cash, enforce zero averaging down, and treat <= $63.00 as a hard breach.

Also note why the snapshot-derived $61.24–$63.10 watch band ($60.96 screen stop) sits below the $63.00 LEAPS floor: that pocket is purely a historical technical support reference carrying 0.0% equity bids. Equity cannot be bought until Uber carves a multi-week Stage 1 base and reclaims $72.40–$73.50 on 1.25x volume, whereas fixed-expiry Dec 2027 LEAPS cannot survive theta decay and gap risk below $63.00.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: SALVAGE CASH BEFORE THE 47-CENT TRIPWIRE SNAPS
book_callouts.text: When out-of-the-money calls expire worthless even at your own Base Case ($75.00), sit 47 cents above a hard floor on 1.63x Stage 4 volume, and face >14% spreads while cash sits at 3.38%, waiting for a bounce is hope—closing into cash is discipline.
